/-!
# Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture

The Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture asks whether every $4$-vertex-connected toroidal graph
has a Hamiltonian cycle. It generalises Tutte's theorem that every $4$-vertex-connected planar
graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.

A graph is *toroidal* if it can be drawn on the torus without crossings. Mathlib has no notion
of a graph embedded in a surface, so this file defines `EmbedsIn G X`: the vertices of `G` are
represented by distinct points of the topological space `X` and the edges by simple arcs, such
that arcs meet only at common endpoints and pass through no other vertex. This is the standard
topological definition of an embedding (see e.g. Mohar–Thomassen, *Graphs on Surfaces*, §2.1).
The torus is the product $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ of two circles.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gr%C3%BCnbaum%E2%80%93Nash-Williams_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Toroidal graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toroidal_graph)
- [Tu56] Tutte, W. T., *A theorem on planar graphs*, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 82 (1956), 99–116.
- [MT01] Mohar, B. and Thomassen, C., *Graphs on Surfaces*, Johns Hopkins University Press
  (2001).
-/

blocks.docstring:
The torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = S^1 \times S^1$, realised as the product of two copies of the
circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `UnitAddCircle`, `AddCircle (1:ℝ)`, `Circle × Circle` (all homeomorphic; `EmbedsIn` is invariant under homeomorphism by `EmbedsIn.of_injective_continuous`).
justification.name: GrunbaumNashWilliamsConjecture.Torus
justification.why_needed: The torus as a topological space: `UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle` (ℝ/ℤ × ℝ/ℤ). Mathlib has no named torus space.

blocks.name: Torus
blocks.text:
/-- The torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = S^1 \times S^1$, realised as the product of two copies of the
circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. -/
abbrev Torus : Type := UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle

def EmbedsIn {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → X) (γ : G.edgeSet → C(unitInterval, X)),
    Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ e, Function.Injective (γ e)) ∧
    (∀ e : G.edgeSet, Sym2.map f e = s(γ e 0, γ e 1)) ∧
    (∀ (e : G.edgeSet) (v : V), f v ∈ Set.range (γ e) → v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)) ∧
    (∀ e e' : G.edgeSet, e ≠ e' → Set.range (γ e) ∩ Set.range (γ e') ⊆ Set.range f)
blocks.docstring:
A simple graph `G` *embeds* in a topological space `X` if there are
* an injective map `f` sending vertices to points of `X`, and
* for each edge `e`, a simple arc `γ e` in `X` (a continuous injective map from $[0,1]$)
  whose endpoints are the images of the two endpoints of `e`,

such that an arc passes through the image of a vertex only at its own endpoints, and two
distinct arcs meet only at images of vertices (hence only at common endpoints).

justification.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib and the repo for planar/toroidal/genus/embedding notions: only `SimpleGraph.Embedding` (graph homomorphisms, unrelated), `UnitDistanceEmbeddable` (metric, not topological), and `IsEmbedding` for maps (used for Jordan curves in InscribedSquare.lean, but not for graphs).
justification.name: GrunbaumNashWilliamsConjecture.EmbedsIn
justification.why_needed: Standard topological notion of a graph embedded in a space X (Mohar–Thomassen §2.1): injective vertex map f : V → X, and for each edge e ∈ G.edgeSet a continuous injective arc γ e : C(unitInterval, X) with `Sym2.map f e = s(γ e 0, γ e 1)`, such that the image of a vertex lies on an arc only if the vertex is an endpoint of that edge, and distinct arcs intersect only in vertex images (hence only in common endpoints). Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has any notion of planar/toroidal graphs or graph embeddings into topological spaces.

blocks.name: EmbedsIn
blocks.text:
/-- A simple graph `G` *embeds* in a topological space `X` if there are
* an injective map `f` sending vertices to points of `X`, and
* for each edge `e`, a simple arc `γ e` in `X` (a continuous injective map from $[0,1]$)
  whose endpoints are the images of the two endpoints of `e`,

such that an arc passes through the image of a vertex only at its own endpoints, and two
distinct arcs meet only at images of vertices (hence only at common endpoints). -/
def EmbedsIn {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → X) (γ : G.edgeSet → C(unitInterval, X)),
    Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ e, Function.Injective (γ e)) ∧
    (∀ e : G.edgeSet, Sym2.map f e = s(γ e 0, γ e 1)) ∧
    (∀ (e : G.edgeSet) (v : V), f v ∈ Set.range (γ e) → v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)) ∧
    (∀ e e' : G.edgeSet, e ≠ e' → Set.range (γ e) ∩ Set.range (γ e') ⊆ Set.range f)

blocks.code:
def IsToroidal {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  EmbedsIn G Torus
blocks.docstring:
A graph is *toroidal* if it embeds in the torus. Every planar graph is toroidal, see
`IsPlanar.isToroidal`.

justification.name: GrunbaumNashWilliamsConjecture.IsToroidal

def IsPlanar {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem EmbedsIn.anti {V : Type*} {G H : SimpleGraph V} {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (hHG : H ≤ G) (hG : EmbedsIn G X) : EmbedsIn H X := by
  obtain ⟨f, γ, hf, hγ, hends, hvert, hdisj⟩ := hG
  refine ⟨f, fun e => γ ⟨e, edgeSet_mono hHG e.2⟩, hf, fun e => hγ _,
    fun e => hends ⟨e, edgeSet_mono hHG e.2⟩,
    fun e v hv => hvert _ v hv, fun e e' hee' => hdisj _ _ fun h => hee' ?_⟩
  exact Subtype.ext congr(($h).1)
blocks.docstring: If `G` embeds in `X` then so does every subgraph of `G` on the same vertex set.

  refine ⟨f, fun e => γ ⟨e, edgeSet_mono hHG e.2⟩, hf, fun e => hγ _,
    fun e => hends ⟨e, edgeSet_mono hHG e.2⟩,

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem EmbedsIn.of_injective_continuous {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}
    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (hG : EmbedsIn G X)
    {φ : X → Y} (hφ : Function.Injective φ) (hφc : Continuous φ) : EmbedsIn G Y := by
  obtain ⟨f, γ, hf, hγ, hends, hvert, hdisj⟩ := hG
  refine ⟨φ ∘ f, fun e => (⟨φ, hφc⟩ : C(X, Y)).comp (γ e), hφ.comp hf,
    fun e => hφ.comp (hγ e), fun e => ?_, fun e v ⟨t, ht⟩ => hvert e v ⟨t, hφ ht⟩,
    fun e e' hee' y ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, ⟨t', ht'⟩⟩ => ?_⟩
  · rw [← Sym2.map_map, hends e, Sym2.map_pair_eq]
    rfl
  · obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hdisj e e' hee' ⟨⟨t, hφ (ht.trans ht'.symm)⟩, ⟨t', rfl⟩⟩
    exact ⟨v, (congrArg φ hv).trans ht'⟩
blocks.docstring: An embedding in `X` composed with a continuous injection `X → Y` is an embedding in `Y`.
blocks.name: EmbedsIn.of_injective_continuous

/-- An embedding in `X` composed with a continuous injection `X → Y` is an embedding in `Y`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem EmbedsIn.of_injective_continuous {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}
    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (hG : EmbedsIn G X)
    {φ : X → Y} (hφ : Function.Injective φ) (hφc : Continuous φ) : EmbedsIn G Y := by
  obtain ⟨f, γ, hf, hγ, hends, hvert, hdisj⟩ := hG
  refine ⟨φ ∘ f, fun e => (⟨φ, hφc⟩ : C(X, Y)).comp (γ e), hφ.comp hf,
    fun e => hφ.comp (hγ e), fun e => ?_, fun e v ⟨t, ht⟩ => hvert e v ⟨t, hφ ht⟩,
    fun e e' hee' y ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, ⟨t', ht'⟩⟩ => ?_⟩
  · rw [← Sym2.map_map, hends e, Sym2.map_pair_eq]
    rfl
  · obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hdisj e e' hee' ⟨⟨t, hφ (ht.trans ht'.symm)⟩, ⟨t', rfl⟩⟩
    exact ⟨v, (congrArg φ hv).trans ht'⟩

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsPlanar.isToroidal {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : IsPlanar G) : IsToroidal G := by
  -- `g` is a continuous injection `ℝ → (0, 1)`, and `(↑)` is injective on `[0, 1)`.
  let g : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => 1 / 2 + Real.arctan x / Real.pi
  have hg : ∀ x, g x ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (0 + 1) := fun x => by
    have h1 := Real.arctan_lt_pi_div_two x
    have h2 := Real.neg_pi_div_two_lt_arctan x
    have hpi := Real.pi_pos
    simp only [g, Set.mem_Ico, zero_add]
    constructor
    · have : -(1 / 2 : ℝ) < Real.arctan x / Real.pi := by
        rw [lt_div_iff₀ hpi]; linarith
      linarith
    · have : Real.arctan x / Real.pi < 1 / 2 := by
        rw [div_lt_iff₀ hpi]; linarith
      linarith
  have hginj : Function.Injective g := fun x y hxy => by
    simpa [g, Real.pi_ne_zero] using hxy
  have hgc : Continuous g := by fun_prop
  let φ : ℝ² → Torus := fun p => ((g (p 0) : UnitAddCircle), (g (p 1) : UnitAddCircle))
  refine hG.of_injective_continuous (φ := φ) (fun p q hpq => ?_) (by fun_prop)
  simp only [φ, Prod.mk.injEq, AddCircle.coe_eq_coe_iff_of_mem_Ico (hg _) (hg _)] at hpq
  ext i
  fin_cases i
  · exact hginj hpq.1
  · exact hginj hpq.2

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_top_fin_two : IsPlanar (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) := by
  let p : ℝ² := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1
  have hp : p ≠ 0 := by
    simp [p]
  have hedge : ∀ e : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).edgeSet, (e : Sym2 (Fin 2)) = s(0, 1) := by
    rintro ⟨e, he⟩
    induction e using Sym2.ind with
    | _ a b =>
      rw [mem_edgeSet, top_adj] at he
      fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> simp_all [Sym2.eq_swap]
  refine ⟨fun i => ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) • p, fun _ => ⟨fun t => (t : ℝ) • p, by fun_prop⟩,
    fun i j hij => ?_, fun e s t hst => ?_, fun e => ?_, fun e v _ => ?_, fun e e' hee' => ?_⟩
  · exact Fin.val_injective (Nat.cast_injective (smul_left_injective ℝ hp hij))
  · exact Subtype.val_injective (smul_left_injective ℝ hp hst)
  · rw [hedge e, Sym2.map_pair_eq]
    simp
  · rw [hedge e]
    fin_cases v <;> simp
  · exact absurd (Subtype.ext ((hedge e).trans (hedge e').symm)) hee'

theorem grunbaum_nash_williams_conjecture :

blocks.docstring:
**Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture.**
Does every $4$-vertex-connected toroidal graph have a Hamiltonian cycle?

Here a finite simple graph is $4$-vertex-connected if it has more than $4$ vertices and remains
connected after the removal of any set of fewer than $4$ vertices (`IsKConnected G 4`); this
excludes the degenerate graphs on at most $4$ vertices. It is toroidal if it can be drawn on the
torus without crossings (`IsToroidal`); planar graphs are included. The conjectured answer is yes.
blocks.name: grunbaum_nash_williams_conjecture

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no Prop (conjectured answer: yes) quantifying over finite simple graphs embeddable in the torus (genus ≤ 1, so planar graphs are included) that are 4-vertex-connected; Mathlib has `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian` and FormalConjecturesForMathlib has a k-connectivity predicate, but toroidal embeddability has no Mathlib notion and needs a bespoke definition, and 4-connectivity should be checked to exclude degenerate graphs with fewer than 5 vertices.
claims.reviewer_why: c01's `EmbedsIn` is a faithful standard topological graph embedding (injective vertex map; per unordered edge a continuous injective arc from [0,1] into the Hausdorff torus UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle, hence a simple arc; endpoint condition via `Sym2.map f e = s(γ e 0, γ e 1)`; arcs contain vertex images only at their endpoints; distinct arcs meet only at vertex images, hence only at common endpoints). `IsToroidal := EmbedsIn G Torus` is genus ≤ 1 (planar graphs included, proven as `IsPlanar.isToroidal`). The statement uses the repo's `IsKConnected G 4` (forces 4 < |V| and connectivity after deleting < 4 vertices, so degenerate small graphs are excluded and Mathlib `IsHamiltonian`'s `card ≠ 1` guard is inert) and the preferred `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) …` form since the source is phrased 'on whether …'; `answer(True)` is the conjectured positive answer. Edits: reordered hypotheses to `IsKConnected G 4 → IsToroidal G` matching the English, dropped the extra solved variants (Tutte, Thomas–Yu, Thomas–Yu–Zang) to ship exactly the slot, trimmed references; kept c01's proven API lemmas and satisfiability tests. c08/c03/c05 were equally sound alternatives (c08 differs only in direct-vs-answer form and adjacency-indexed arcs with a symmetry condition; c03/c05 use direct form). c02 sound but uses `letI := Classical.decEq V` inside the proposition; c06 has unconstrained duplicate arcs per oriented edge (logically equivalent but unclean); c07 uses `Quot.out` for endpoints; c04's rotation-system definition is correct for connected graphs but wrongly bakes `G.Connected` into 'toroidal' and needs `DecidableRel G.Adj`.

context:
In graph theory, the Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture states that every 4-vertex-connected toroidal graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. It is a generalization of Tutte's theorem on Hamiltonian cycles, according to which every 4-vertex-connected planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. An analogous theorem of Thomas and Yu holds for graphs on the projective plane.
For 4-vertex-connected planar and projective planar graphs, more strongly, every edge belongs to a Hamiltonian cycle. However, this stronger property is not true of toroidal graphs. For instance, the Cartesian product of two even cycles, with a diagonal added to one of its  quadrilateral faces, is a 4-vertex-connected toroidal graph none of whose Hamiltonian cycles contains the added diagonal.
The conjecture was formulated in the early 1970s by Branko Grünbaum and Crispin Nash-Williams. As partial progress toward the conjecture, Robin Thomas and X. Yu proved that every 5-vertex-connected toroidal graph has a Hamiltonian cycle, and (with W. Zang) that every 4-vertex-connected toroidal graph has a Hamiltonian path.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition is correct; the notes (planar graphs included, need for a bespoke toroidal definition, 4-connectivity excluding small graphs) all match what was formalized.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture

The Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture asks whether every $4$-vertex-connected toroidal graph
has a Hamiltonian cycle. It generalises Tutte's theorem that every $4$-vertex-connected planar
graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.

A graph is *toroidal* if it can be drawn on the torus without crossings. Mathlib has no notion
of a graph embedded in a surface, so this file defines `EmbedsIn G X`: the vertices of `G` are
represented by distinct points of the topological space `X` and the edges by simple arcs, such
that arcs meet only at common endpoints and pass through no other vertex. This is the standard
topological definition of an embedding (see e.g. Mohar–Thomassen, *Graphs on Surfaces*, §2.1).
The torus is the product $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ of two circles.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gr%C3%BCnbaum%E2%80%93Nash-Williams_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Toroidal graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toroidal_graph)
- [Tu56] Tutte, W. T., *A theorem on planar graphs*, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 82 (1956), 99–116.
- [MT01] Mohar, B. and Thomassen, C., *Graphs on Surfaces*, Johns Hopkins University Press
  (2001).
-/

namespace GrunbaumNashWilliamsConjecture

open SimpleGraph
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/-- The torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = S^1 \times S^1$, realised as the product of two copies of the
circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. -/
abbrev Torus : Type := UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle

/-- A simple graph `G` *embeds* in a topological space `X` if there are
* an injective map `f` sending vertices to points of `X`, and
* for each edge `e`, a simple arc `γ e` in `X` (a continuous injective map from $[0,1]$)
  whose endpoints are the images of the two endpoints of `e`,

such that an arc passes through the image of a vertex only at its own endpoints, and two
distinct arcs meet only at images of vertices (hence only at common endpoints). -/
def EmbedsIn {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → X) (γ : G.edgeSet → C(unitInterval, X)),
    Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ e, Function.Injective (γ e)) ∧
    (∀ e : G.edgeSet, Sym2.map f e = s(γ e 0, γ e 1)) ∧
    (∀ (e : G.edgeSet) (v : V), f v ∈ Set.range (γ e) → v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)) ∧
    (∀ e e' : G.edgeSet, e ≠ e' → Set.range (γ e) ∩ Set.range (γ e') ⊆ Set.range f)

/-- A graph is *toroidal* if it embeds in the torus. Every planar graph is toroidal, see
`IsPlanar.isToroidal`. -/
def IsToroidal {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  EmbedsIn G Torus

/-- A graph is *planar* if it embeds in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. -/
def IsPlanar {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  EmbedsIn G ℝ²

/-- If `G` embeds in `X` then so does every subgraph of `G` on the same vertex set. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem EmbedsIn.anti {V : Type*} {G H : SimpleGraph V} {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (hHG : H ≤ G) (hG : EmbedsIn G X) : EmbedsIn H X := by
  obtain ⟨f, γ, hf, hγ, hends, hvert, hdisj⟩ := hG
  refine ⟨f, fun e => γ ⟨e, edgeSet_mono hHG e.2⟩, hf, fun e => hγ _,
    fun e => hends ⟨e, edgeSet_mono hHG e.2⟩,
    fun e v hv => hvert _ v hv, fun e e' hee' => hdisj _ _ fun h => hee' ?_⟩
  exact Subtype.ext congr(($h).1)

/-- An embedding in `X` composed with a continuous injection `X → Y` is an embedding in `Y`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem EmbedsIn.of_injective_continuous {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}
    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (hG : EmbedsIn G X)
    {φ : X → Y} (hφ : Function.Injective φ) (hφc : Continuous φ) : EmbedsIn G Y := by
  obtain ⟨f, γ, hf, hγ, hends, hvert, hdisj⟩ := hG
  refine ⟨φ ∘ f, fun e => (⟨φ, hφc⟩ : C(X, Y)).comp (γ e), hφ.comp hf,
    fun e => hφ.comp (hγ e), fun e => ?_, fun e v ⟨t, ht⟩ => hvert e v ⟨t, hφ ht⟩,
    fun e e' hee' y ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, ⟨t', ht'⟩⟩ => ?_⟩
  · rw [← Sym2.map_map, hends e, Sym2.map_pair_eq]
    rfl
  · obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hdisj e e' hee' ⟨⟨t, hφ (ht.trans ht'.symm)⟩, ⟨t', rfl⟩⟩
    exact ⟨v, (congrArg φ hv).trans ht'⟩

/-- Every planar graph is toroidal: the plane embeds in the torus. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsPlanar.isToroidal {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : IsPlanar G) : IsToroidal G := by
  -- `g` is a continuous injection `ℝ → (0, 1)`, and `(↑)` is injective on `[0, 1)`.
  let g : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => 1 / 2 + Real.arctan x / Real.pi
  have hg : ∀ x, g x ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (0 + 1) := fun x => by
    have h1 := Real.arctan_lt_pi_div_two x
    have h2 := Real.neg_pi_div_two_lt_arctan x
    have hpi := Real.pi_pos
    simp only [g, Set.mem_Ico, zero_add]
    constructor
    · have : -(1 / 2 : ℝ) < Real.arctan x / Real.pi := by
        rw [lt_div_iff₀ hpi]; linarith
      linarith
    · have : Real.arctan x / Real.pi < 1 / 2 := by
        rw [div_lt_iff₀ hpi]; linarith
      linarith
  have hginj : Function.Injective g := fun x y hxy => by
    simpa [g, Real.pi_ne_zero] using hxy
  have hgc : Continuous g := by fun_prop
  let φ : ℝ² → Torus := fun p => ((g (p 0) : UnitAddCircle), (g (p 1) : UnitAddCircle))
  refine hG.of_injective_continuous (φ := φ) (fun p q hpq => ?_) (by fun_prop)
  simp only [φ, Prod.mk.injEq, AddCircle.coe_eq_coe_iff_of_mem_Ico (hg _) (hg _)] at hpq
  ext i
  fin_cases i
  · exact hginj hpq.1
  · exact hginj hpq.2

/-- A single edge is planar: the definition of `EmbedsIn` is satisfiable. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_top_fin_two : IsPlanar (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) := by
  let p : ℝ² := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1
  have hp : p ≠ 0 := by
    simp [p]
  have hedge : ∀ e : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).edgeSet, (e : Sym2 (Fin 2)) = s(0, 1) := by
    rintro ⟨e, he⟩
    induction e using Sym2.ind with
    | _ a b =>
      rw [mem_edgeSet, top_adj] at he
      fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> simp_all [Sym2.eq_swap]
  refine ⟨fun i => ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) • p, fun _ => ⟨fun t => (t : ℝ) • p, by fun_prop⟩,
    fun i j hij => ?_, fun e s t hst => ?_, fun e => ?_, fun e v _ => ?_, fun e e' hee' => ?_⟩
  · exact Fin.val_injective (Nat.cast_injective (smul_left_injective ℝ hp hij))
  · exact Subtype.val_injective (smul_left_injective ℝ hp hst)
  · rw [hedge e, Sym2.map_pair_eq]
    simp
  · rw [hedge e]
    fin_cases v <;> simp
  · exact absurd (Subtype.ext ((hedge e).trans (hedge e').symm)) hee'

/-- A single edge is toroidal. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isToroidal_top_fin_two : IsToroidal (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) :=
  isPlanar_top_fin_two.isToroidal

/--
**Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture.**
Does every $4$-vertex-connected toroidal graph have a Hamiltonian cycle?

Here a finite simple graph is $4$-vertex-connected if it has more than $4$ vertices and remains
connected after the removal of any set of fewer than $4$ vertices (`IsKConnected G 4`); this
excludes the degenerate graphs on at most $4$ vertices. It is toroidal if it can be drawn on the
torus without crossings (`IsToroidal`); planar graphs are included. The conjectured answer is yes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem grunbaum_nash_williams_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      IsKConnected G 4 → IsToroidal G → G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

end GrunbaumNashWilliamsConjecture

items: The list-page entry is phrased as a question ('whether ...'), so the slot uses `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ...`; `answer(True)` is the conjectured positive answer.

'Toroidal graph' is formalized by the standard topological definition (embeddable in the torus without crossings) via bespoke `EmbedsIn`; the torus is `UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle`. Planar graphs are therefore toroidal, which is proved (not sorried) as `IsPlanar.isToroidal` using an explicit continuous injection ℝ² → torus.

Arcs are indexed by `G.edgeSet` (unordered pairs) with endpoint condition `Sym2.map f e = s(γ e 0, γ e 1)`, avoiding the need for a consistency condition between `arc u v` and `arc v u`. Arcs are continuous injective maps from `unitInterval`; in Hausdorff spaces (torus, plane) these are exactly simple arcs.

Graphs are finite simple graphs (`SimpleGraph V`, `[Fintype V]`, `V : Type`). Loops/multi-edges are irrelevant to Hamiltonicity and connectivity, and every finite graph is isomorphic to one with vertex type in `Type`, so nothing is lost. `[DecidableEq V]` is required by Mathlib's `IsHamiltonian`.

4-vertex-connectivity is the repo's `IsKConnected G 4`: `4 < Fintype.card V ∧ ∀ S : Finset V, S.card < 4 → (G.induce Sᶜ).Connected`. This matches Diestel's definition and excludes degenerate graphs with ≤ 4 vertices (e.g. K₄), as the decomposition notes ask.
Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian` is `Fintype.card V ≠ 1 → ∃ a p, p.IsHamiltonianCycle`; the guard is vacuous here since 4-connectivity forces ≥ 5 vertices.

Beyond the single slot, the file also states three closely related solved results from the Wikipedia article as `research solved` variants (Tutte's theorem for planar graphs, Thomas–Yu for 5-connected toroidal graphs, Thomas–Yu–Zang Hamiltonian paths for 4-connected toroidal graphs), plus proved API lemmas (`EmbedsIn.anti`, `EmbedsIn.of_injective_continuous`, `IsPlanar.isToroidal`) and proved tests that a single edge is planar/toroidal (checking `EmbedsIn` is satisfiable). Reviewers may want to move `EmbedsIn`/`IsPlanar`/`IsToroidal` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib; they were kept in the problem file because the task restricts output to one file.
